rail_guard.text: Oxford Station. The trains to everywhere you have been, and to the Gloucester Road, the Great Western and a surprising number of places that are not Oxford.
You'll need a Rail Pass. I'll ask nicely, and then I'll ask the barrier.

ox_guide.text: Welcome to Carfax, the crossing at the middle of Oxford. 'Carfax' is from the Latin for four-forked. Four roads, one tower, and two thousand people photographing it.
That's not the main tower, by the way. People always point at the wrong spire. There are about a hundred. Choose one and look amazed.

ox_busker.text: They don't let you busk on the cobbles by the Camera, which is a pity. The acoustic is superb and so are the tourists. I do my fiddling here, with an eye out for the Proctors.

The University has a pair of Proctors, who walk the streets in black gowns and white bow ties, with two helpers called Bulldogs in bowler hats. They're allowed to arrest students. They mostly just say hello.

ox_bookseller.text: Oxford University Press is one of the oldest university presses in the world, and there are more bookshops here than I can count, and I try. Blackwell's has a floor called the Norrington Room, with three miles of shelves.
Nobody reads the whole of any shelf. They look, they sigh, they buy a postcard. It's a lovely life.

ox_runner.text: I run the towpath along the Thames. The college boathouses are all along it, and in Eights Week the eights bump each other, which is a rowing race where you try to hit the boat in front. Gentle, it isn't.
Cox shouts. Everyone else is busy. It's a good arrangement.

ox_cherwell.text: The Cherwell comes down from Northamptonshire and joins the Thames here. It's called 'Charwell', not 'Cherwell', by anyone who went to school nearby.
That's the sort of thing Oxford does. Magdalen is 'Maudlin' and Cherwell is 'Charwell'. Nobody says it right on purpose.

ox_bobby.text: Christ Church Meadow has had cattle in it since before the college. They are Longhorns, so you'll have to give way. The cows have the right of way, the Dean has the right of way and the Dean's cat has it, too.
The Meadow is the loveliest walk in the city. Sometimes the river floods it. Then it's a different walk.

ox_poet.text: 'That sweet city with her dreaming spires.' Matthew Arnold, 1866. I have it on a mug.
The spires are not all dreaming, by the way. Some of them are leaning on cranes. Preservation is a long job.

ox_pancake_marshal.text: Frying pan, apron, headscarf. That is the whole kit list, and the headscarf is not optional. The vicar is very firm.
